Where it began

Rajat Patidar was born in Indore, in Madhya Pradesh, on 1 June 1993. He joined a cricket club at eight, and it was his grandfather who later signed him up for an academy, a decision that paid off handsomely.

The young Patidar was a bowler first. Only after his under-15 years did he turn his full attention to batting, though he kept his off-spin as a handy second string.

The player

He made his first-class debut for Madhya Pradesh in the Ranji Trophy in October 2015. In the 2018–19 season he was his side's top run-scorer, with 713 runs from eight matches, and against Haryana he once reached a hundred from just 68 balls on the way to 159.

India came calling for one-day cricket, and his ODI debut arrived in December 2023 against South Africa. Two months later, with Virat Kohli missing the opening Tests against England, Patidar was called into the Test squad and made his debut at the start of February 2024. By November 2026 he had played 3 Tests, scoring 63 runs with a best of 32, and held 4 catches. It was a brief taste of Test cricket, but a cap is a cap, and it is his for life.

What made him special

Patidar is a right-hander built for momentum. When he gets going the ball travels fast and far, and he can change the mood of a match in a handful of overs. In the 2024–25 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, captaining Madhya Pradesh, he scored 428 runs at better than a run and three quarters a ball, and dragged his side to the final.

The Test numbers are the one part of the story that never quite took off. Six innings is a small window, and the longer game never saw the batter that domestic bowlers came to know so well.

Away from the middle

His name is tied to Royal Challengers Bengaluru. In 2022, signed as a mid-season replacement after going unsold at the auction, he made an unbeaten 112 in the Eliminator against Lucknow. No uncapped player had scored a hundred in an IPL play-off before.

In 2025 he was made captain, and Bengaluru won their first IPL title. A year later they won it again, and he had his best season with the bat, 501 runs at a strike rate of 192.36. Only two captains before him had won back-to-back titles: MS Dhoni and Rohit Sharma.

And finally

Bengaluru released him after his first season and nobody bought him at the next auction. By 2026 he had lifted the trophy twice as their captain. Few cricketers can claim a more satisfying answer to being overlooked.
